data.description:
Investors who take an interest in B&G Foods, Inc. (NYSE:BGS) should definitely note that the President, Robert Mills, recently paid US$3.60 per share to buy US$250k worth of the stock. That's a very decent purchase to our minds and it grew their holding by a solid 30%.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

B&G Foods Insider Transactions Over The Last Year

In fact, the recent purchase by Robert Mills was the biggest purchase of B&G Foods shares made by an insider individual in the last twelve months, according to our records. That implies that an insider found the current price of US$3.63 per share to be enticing. Of course they may have changed their mind. But this suggests they are optimistic. While we always like to see insider buying, it's less meaningful if the purchases were made at much lower prices, as the opportunity they saw may have passed. Happily, the B&G Foods insiders decided to buy shares at close to current prices.

Over the last year, we can see that insiders have bought 75.06k shares worth US$268k. But they sold 77.18k shares for US$378k. In total, B&G Foods insiders sold more than they bought over the last year. You can see the insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last year depicted in the chart below. Does B&G Foods Boast High Insider Ownership?

Another way to test the alignment between the leaders of a company and other shareholders is to look at how many shares they own. We usually like to see fairly high levels of insider ownership. Insiders own 5.2% of B&G Foods shares, worth about US$14m. Anyone interested in Park-Ohio Holdings Corp. (NASDAQ:PKOH) should probably be aware that the VP & CFO, Patrick Fogarty, recently divested US$254k worth of shares in the company, at an average price of US$43.32 each. On the bright side, that sale was only 4.1% of their holding, so we doubt it's very meaningful, on its own.

The Last 12 Months Of Insider Transactions At Park-Ohio Holdings

In the last twelve months, the biggest single sale by an insider was when the Chief Legal & Administrative Officer and Corporate Secretary, Robert Vilsack, sold US$600k worth of shares at a price of US$50.14 per share. We generally don't like to see insider selling, but the lower the sale price, the more it concerns us. The silver lining is that this sell-down took place above the latest price (US$40.89). So it may not shed much light on insider confidence at current levels.

Does Park-Ohio Holdings Boast High Insider Ownership?

I like to look at how many shares insiders own in a company, to help inform my view of how aligned they are with insiders. We usually like to see fairly high levels of insider ownership. Park-Ohio Holdings insiders own 30% of the company, currently worth about US$181m based on the recent share price. I like to see this level of insider ownership, because it increases the chances that management are thinking about the best interests of shareholders.

So What Do The Park-Ohio Holdings Insider Transactions Indicate?

Insiders sold stock recently, but they haven't been buying. Looking to the last twelve months, our data doesn't show any insider buying. But since Park-Ohio Holdings is profitable and growing, we're not too worried by this. It is good to see high insider ownership, but the insider selling leaves us cautious.
